Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
Sri Rajesh Kumar Jaiswal learned counsel has put in appearance on behalf of the respondent no.2.

This is a wholly misconceived petition seeking a writ of mandamus commanding the respondent nos.2 and 3 namely National Highway Authority and State respondents to pay compensation to the writ petitioner in accordance with the Clause 4.6(iii)(a) of the Government Order dated 28.12.2017.

sentences.text:
Reference to sub clause iii(a) of Clause 4.6 of the Government Order dated 28.12.2017 has been made by the learned counsel for the petitioner to assert that though award was declared in the year,
2012 but compensation had not been paid for majority of land holding under acquisition as on 31.12.2014. The respondents, thus, are liable to pay compensation in accordance with the first schedule of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
On a pointed query made by the Court as to how the petitioner is entitled for the benefit of the said clause, reference has been made to para-16 of the writ petition which reads as under:-
"16.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: That all the land owners/farmers of village mauja Viraili had been paid compensation in June, 2016 after the effectiveness of the new Land Acquisition Act (RFCTLARR Act), 2013 since 01.01.2015."

There is no description in the writ petition with respect to the area for which the award had been declared, the extent of the lands for which compensation had been paid to the tenure holder whether the compensation had been deposited by the competent authority.
Vague assertion that most of the land holders had been paid compensation in the month of June, 2016 is not sufficient to entertain the writ petition.

For the vague statement made in the writ petition with regard to the payment of compensation to land holders, affected by the acquisition in question, in writ petition filed in the month of February,
2023, we do not find any good ground to issue any mandamus.
For the above, the writ petition is dismissed being misconceived.
